boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Mansura record (May 16, 1864) in the Red River Campaign [March-April 1864]. The frozen campaign label reads March-April 1864 and the live date field reads 'March-April 1864'; neither replaces the record's frozen dates. The May 15 fighting at Marksville and the May 17 attacks near Moreauville are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, river operations and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Banks's Red River Expeditionary Force [US] and District of West Louisiana [CS]; the live field reads zero. Taylor's May 16 dispatch says the enemy probably had 16,000 men on the field and perhaps more, and lists nineteen guns on his right and thirteen on his left; on May 14 he wrote of his little force against four times their number, and on May 10 of scarce 6,000 men. Irwin says the disparity in numbers was too great for Taylor to do more than make a show of resistance, and lists the Union infantry divisions in line.
claims.rationale: Interested estimates from different dates and a retrospective judgment; no return. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

open_questions: Banks's report, Lawler's (No. 10), A. J. Smith's, Emory's, Arnold's and Fordham's reports, Faries's artillery report (No. 103), W. Steele's report (No. 101) and the returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Richard B. Irwin's History of the Nineteenth Army Corps (Putnam's, 1892) is a retrospective history by the former assistant adjutant-general of the corps and of Banks's Department of the Gulf, an interested Union account; it cites the Official Records and gives Taylor's and Kirby Smith's figures, so it is not independent of them. Taylor's April 18, 1864 report, his March 13-14 letters printed as its inclosures, his April 24-May 19 dispatches and his April 11 general order are one family of interested Confederate accounts. Official Records Series I, Volume XXXIV, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
